correctnessFindings.assessment: The event array now trims immediately after append to the existing MAX_EVENTS=10000 limit. Aggregates are still updated for every recorded event; the 2000-entry counted-PR deduplication policy is unchanged.
Serialization already retained only the newest 10000 events. Moving that trim before asynchronous persistence bounds memory while a write is stalled without reducing the configured persisted history.

originalReview.userVisibleBeforeAfter: Normal statistics summaries and persisted event capacity remain unchanged. During a prolonged stalled write, old raw events leave the in-memory array earlier; cumulative counts and totals remain updated.
originalReview.capacityAndDataLoss: Existing 10000 raw-event capacity is enforced earlier; no new aggregate or persisted-history quota. The class summary API returns aggregates rather than exposing the transient unbounded event array.

platformEvidence.assessment: Plain array and aggregate operations have the same JavaScript semantics on macOS, Linux, and Windows. Existing filesystem persistence behavior is not replaced. The fresh Node tests ran on macOS; Linux/Windows execution is not claimed.
platformEvidence.executedHost: Fresh shared batch: macOS darwin arm64; Node 26.6.0. PRs outside that batch have no new execution in this follow-up.
